quiver: A quick, small movement, as when you are cold or afraid.
cockleshell: The shell of a small sea animal, used here to make a border round a small water garden.
sty: A small building on a farm for fat animals with short legs, kept for their meat.
eaves: The lower edges of the top of a house, which hang out over the wall.
vaporous: Full of thin white air that is hard to see through.
valerian: A plant that grows on old walls and has small red-white flower heads.
sheaf: A group of cut grain plants, held together.
humbug: A person who says things he does not mean, to make people believe him.
gorse: A wild plant with yellow flower heads and sharp points.
mutinously: In a way that will not do what you are told.
paling: One of the pointed sticks that stand up in a line around a garden.
carouse: Drinking and having fun in a loud way with others.
trifle: A soft, sweet food made with fruit and sweet milk.
